recipes.name: No Bake Cookies without Peanut Butter

steps.text: Place sugar, butter, and milk in a medium saucepan. Bring to a rolling boil over medium-low heat; boil for one minute, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and mix in oats, cocoa powder, and vanilla. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper. Let cool until hardened.

raw_recipe.headline: No Bake Cookies without Peanut Butter
raw_recipe.description: These no-bake cookies are made without peanut butter. This recipe requires just sugar, butter, milk, cocoa, oats, and vanilla for a quick treat.
raw_recipe.name: No Bake Cookies without Peanut Butter

Remove from heat and mix in oats, cocoa powder, and vanilla. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto waxed paper. Let cool until hardened.

review.reviewBody: I wanted to make these cookies but I couldn't get in touch with my mom for the recipe. This is exactly how I remember them growing up. A few tips for people who said these were a gooey mess or very crumbly: When ever you heat Sugar, you are using the science of candy making, which allows for the heating of sugar to very particular temperatures, and since many stoves very in temperature, relying on 1 minute of boiling may not work for everyone so try this: Remember the stages of sugar making Thread: 230-235 (This will make a syrup) Soft Ball: 335-240 (This is the stage we will concentrate on for making these cookies) firm ball: 245-250 hard ball 250- 265 Soft crack- 270-290 hard crack- 300-310 For this particular recipe, after 1 minute of boiling, get a cup of cold water and drop a small spoon full of the syrup into the batter. If it forms a small, soft ball in the water, take it off the heat. If it creates a stringy thread, it's not done yet.

This recipe is delicious! I made it because I wanted to try no-bakes without peanut butter. The cookies were pretty gooey when I started spooning out on the pans. I added a half a cup more of oats and they set up beautifully. One important step this recipe skips over is letting them cool in the fridge for at least an hour.

Followed the recipe with a bit of changes ;) for one, followed another reviewers adjustment of boiling (on med-high heat) the Sugar, butter, milk and cocoa powder, but I went ahead and added the 1tsp of flavor (which i used 1/2 tsp of vanilla extract and 1/2 tsp of butter extract). I boiled for 5 mins stirring very often. In another bowl I put in the 3 cups of quick oats, with just two handfuls of mini marshmallows, 1 cup of semi sweet chocolate chips and 1/2 cup of chopped pecans then tossed well using my hands. I added the hot mixture to the dry and mixed well with a spoon. I had cookie sheets with parchment paper that I just lightly sprayed with Canola Oil. Dropped the mixture by the spoonfuls and let set for just a min or two, buy then it was cool enough for me to form the mixture into perfect little circle/disks. I let cool to room temp for apprx. 10 mins (ate one, just as a test ;) while it was still a little warm. It had a very little crumble to it and it was soft and chewy but formed perfectly) Oh! then stuck them in the refrigerator till dinner time. They are absolutely delicious and oh so sweet (enough to satisfy my sweet tooth!). Hope this helps. Happy Baking!

I think the key word that is missing in this recipe is ‘rolling’ boil. When cooking the milk, butter, sugar, and (I also boiled the cocoa with this) it needs to not just boil, but be at a rolling boil and then start counting a minute. My mom always explained to me, that a rolling boil, is one where no matter how much you stir, the bubbles don’t go away. I have never had this recipe fail - I have eaten them before they set up a few times - because I couldn’t wait! My recipe calls for 1/2 c. Coconut too (but not everyone likes that)

Excellent recipe. I actually bought a candy thermometer just for this recipe. That made all the difference. 235F for FIVE minutes, not one minute. Turned out perfectly! Plus, after adding the oats and stirring them in, I added 2 oz of finely chopped walnuts. Tasty :)

Vegan modifications: Made for my niece, who can't eat dairy. Used unsweetened almond milk, nucoa dairy free buttery sticks, added 1 cup oats, and increased cocoa to 1/2 cup. Because almond milk never reaches soft ball stage, needed to compensate for soupiness with extra oats, and needed more cocoa because extra oats diluted chocolate flavor. They will seem gooey, but will harden up nicely if left overnight. I also make these according to the recipe, turn out just like the ones mom and I made when I was a kid.

There are 2 temperatures you have to get right for your cookies to come out right. The first is the stove temperature. You want the sugar mixture to come to a boil very slowly so all the sugar dissolves. My stove dial has numbers 1 -9 with 5 being medium. I set my temperature half-way between 5 and 6. The second is the sugar mixture temperature. I let mine boil until it reached 235 degrees F. The cookies set up quickly and tasted like I remembered growing up.

This recipe is a favorite in my family for years. My mother's recipe is slightly different. In the saucepan goes the sugar, butter, milk and vanilla. I also add a 1/2 cup of corn syrup to the pot (add syrup when everything is melted). Slowly heat until you don't feel the grit of the sugar, once the sugar is fully liquified, turn up the heat a little more and bring just to a slight boil on the edges of the saucepan. Take off immediately and pour into oat mixture (I use 4 cups oatmeal, 1 cup shredded coconut, 4 heaping tbsp cocoa powder, already mixed in a large bowl). Drop by spoonful and let sit at least one hour. They should turn out perfect.

This is a great recipe. The only big mistake is the cooking time after it comes to a boil. It takes 4 minutes for the chocolate mixture to make a coookie that dries up and doesn’t remain just gooey. Come on cooks you should know better than to think 1 minute would be enough to create a candy mixture.
I used crunchy peanut butter instead bc I like nuts and I boiled for 3 minutes instead of 1. They are great just like my mother used to make them!

This is a recipe I've been using for years. When making the cookie I blend and boil the sugar 1 1/2 cups instead of two. Use Imperial margarine not real butter bring it to rolling boil that can't be stirred down then start timing of 1 minute. Turn off burner and add oats and stir well to coat. Drop by Tablespoon full onto wax paper. Enjoy
We changed 3 cups oats for 2 cups oats & 1 cup sweetened coconut. YUM!!!

me and my little brothers (three and seven) made this one time, and they are DELICIOUS!!! the first time i made them they weren't thick enough so i added just a little bit of peanut butter and they were perfect! thank you so much! i make these a lot and (this is a different time) i used 1 1/2 cups white sugar and 1/2 cup brown sugar to thicken it up because i used almond milk. (DON'T TRY THIS!!!! I didn't know brown sugar has more moisture and they did not set up right.) (still delicious though! : p)
Perfect every time!
Wonderful, I finally found grandma's recipe. Thought I lost it forever in our last move, and grandma and mom are gone.

I tried this recipe to use some different extracts. Without the peanut butter it allowed the other flavors come through. I used cinnamon and they are good! Might be a little too much sugar, so will try and tweak. Also, remember it has to get to 230F in order to set properly. Forget about the 1 min timing. I also am going to try gluten free oats next time. A lot of possibilities!

I made these and followed directions exactly as the recipe called for. I believe the mistake was not boiling the liquid mixture long enough. The recipe says to boil for one minute after the mixture comes to a rolling boil. I think you should boil it longer. Mine did not form correctly, and were gooey. The did not harden. I was a bit disappointed although they did taste good.

Im going on like my sixth batch of these since making them for the holidays and giving many away. You do have to boil linger then a minute. Another review mentioned candy temps and that is very true. And its needs to be a rolling / high boil or they wont set up right. They come out perfect every time for me! Trying them with black cocoa powder today for deeper flavor. And I always make a double batch! One of my favs!
Super easy to make and super yummy! I tend to make big cookies so I get about 12-16 depending.
I've loved this Recipe every since they were made with Peanut butter: but I want to try it now on my Own by making them without the Peanut butter in them; also because I'm a Diabetic
